findings.summary: A start-up file named in the starting shell's environment and the shell's trace option still reached the run, and tracing printed every secret; fixed by restarting under an empty environment in 41bbe67 and 6d38b84.
An exported variable with the same name as the script's own secret array makes the run fail closed with exit 3, changing nothing.

Systems Manager runs the script with sh, which is dash on Ubuntu, so the bash-only script would have stopped at its first bash-only line; fixed by a POSIX start-up block that hands over to bash in 6d38b84.
A stray directory with the temporary link's name in the release root makes the link update land inside it, and the success line prints while the current-release name is a folder, not a link.

When bash starts the script, exported functions named like commands the start-up block uses can skip the hand-over and keep a dirty variable; Systems Manager starts it with sh, which imports no functions, and the limit is recorded in the script header.
The CI log does not name the shell the sh test ran under, so dash is inferred from the test count, and the unset line has only a static test because the hand-over already empties the environment.
The restart under an empty environment also removes the home folder variable, and whether Docker and the secret client cope with that is shown only by the human's first deploy.
